newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Luxembourg's PM sees EMU starting on time.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg's PM sees EMU starting on time.

text.p: Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said on Friday he had no doubt European Union members would decide in 1998 which states would qualify for economic and monetary union (EMU) and the single currency.
He said at a meeting with bankers he also had no doubt the new currency, named the euro, would be introduced on January 1, 1999 so that EMU would start as planned.
He called on EU leaders to interpret the EMU entry criteria as defined in the Maastricht Treaty strictly.
"States which want to join (EMU) must prove that their policies are long-term," he said.

There have been worries recently that the use of one-off policy measures by EU members to meet the Maastricht criteria would run into opposition from some states which fear a relapse by the others, once they are in EMU, could jeopardise the stability of EMU.

Juncker said that, despite Belgium's state debt being well in excess of the Maastricht norm, he said he was convinced the neighbouring country, with which Luxembourg is in a long-standing currency union, would qualify for EMU.

Juncker pointed to Belgium's primary surplus -- the balance between government revenues and spending, excluding debt service costs -- which at around five percent was the highest in Europe and should help it cut debt at an increasing pace.
